I bought and quickly got refunded X: Rebirth on Steam. My main but not only reason was that the game ignores Windows' own screen calibration. Hardly anyone ever uses it, I guess, at least among gamers. But my screen has linear gamma, so I had to rape the screen calibration somewhat to get a proper 1.8 (or 0.55) gamma. Works all throughout Windows, applications, and almost all games. Games that don't support it, which are really rare (Boo, Egosoft!), show their graphics in a very ugly too bright way. Not just the gamma-turned-up-too-much way that all knowledgeable folks now imagine, but something so ugly, it must have had a wrong gamma already somewhere in the render pipeline, not just at the end.

A word about Steam, though: I'm a happy Steam customer (Germany) with almost 1000 games on Steam alone, and all support so far that would indeed concern Valve has been handled to my satisfaction. My 3 or so refunds so far with the new policy have also all gone through. My experience with Valve/Steam so far was that they created a comfortable meadow for a sheep like me to live in and are extremely hands-off except if you ask them to intervene.
